questions.accessible_text:
1. [Maximum mark: 6]

The following Venn diagram shows the events A and B, where P(A)=0.3. The values shown are probabilities.

[Diagram: A-only region 0.1; intersection A∩B labelled p; B-only region labelled q; outside both circles 0.4.]

(a) Find the value of p. [2]

(b) Find the value of q. [2]

(c) Find P(A′∪B). [2]
questions.summary: Use a Venn diagram with A-only probability 0.1, intersection p, B-only q and outside probability 0.4 to find p, q and P(A′∪B).
questions.solution: (a) P(A)=0.1+p=0.3, so p=0.2. (b) The four disjoint regions total 1: 0.1+0.2+q+0.4=1, hence q=0.3. (c) A′∪B excludes only the A-only region, whose probability is 0.1. Therefore P(A′∪B)=1−0.1=0.9.

2. [Maximum mark: 6]

A line L₁ has equation r=(−3,9,10)+s(6,0,2). Point P(15,9,c) lies on L₁. (a) Find c. [4] A second line L₂ is parallel to L₁ and passes through (1,2,3). (b) Write a vector equation for L₂. [2]
questions.summary: A line L₁ has equation r=(−3,9,10)+s(6,0,2). Point P(15,9,c) lies on L₁. (a) Find c. [4] A second line L₂ is parallel to L₁ and passes through (1,2,3). (b) Write a vector equation
questions.solution: (a) From −3+6s=15, s=3, so c=10+2(3)=16. (b) A parallel line is L₂: r=(1,2,3)+t(6,0,2), t∈ℝ. This agrees with the official markscheme.

3. [Maximum mark: 7]

A right triangle ABC has D on AB such that CD bisects angle ACB. [Diagram not to scale: right angle at A; ACD=DCB=θ; AC=14 cm.] (a) Given sinθ=3/5, find cosθ. [3] (b) Find cos2θ. [2] (c) Hence find BC. [2]
questions.summary: A right triangle ABC has D on AB such that CD bisects angle ACB. [Diagram not to scale: right angle at A; ACD=DCB=θ; AC=14 cm.] (a) Given sinθ=3/5, find cosθ. [3] (b) Find cos2θ. [
questions.solution: (a) cosθ=4/5. (b) cos2θ=16/25−9/25=7/25. (c) cos(2θ)=AC/BC, so 7/25=14/BC and BC=50 cm. This agrees with the official markscheme.

questions.accessible_text:
4. [Maximum mark: 6]

Let f(x)=(2x−1)/(x+3), x≠−3. (a) Write the vertical asymptote. [1] (b) Find f⁻¹(x). [3] (c) Find the horizontal asymptote of f⁻¹. [2]
questions.summary: Let f(x)=(2x−1)/(x+3), x≠−3. (a) Write the vertical asymptote. [1] (b) Find f⁻¹(x). [3] (c) Find the horizontal asymptote of f⁻¹. [2]
questions.solution: (a) x=−3. (b) Interchanging x,y and rearranging gives f⁻¹(x)=(3x+1)/(2−x). (c) y=−3. This agrees with the official markscheme.

questions.accessible_text:
5. [Maximum mark: 5]

The derivative of f is f′(x)=2e^(−3x). The graph passes through (1/3,5). Find f(x).
questions.summary: The derivative of f is f′(x)=2e^(−3x). The graph passes through (1/3,5). Find f(x).
questions.solution: f(x)=−(2/3)e^(−3x)+C. Using f(1/3)=5 gives C=5+2/(3e), so f(x)=−(2/3)e^(−3x)+5+2/(3e). This agrees with the official markscheme.

questions.accessible_text:
6. [Maximum mark: 7]

The magnitudes of vectors u and v are 4 and 3, and the angle between them is π/6. Let w=u−v. Find |w|.
questions.summary: The magnitudes of vectors u and v are 4 and 3, and the angle between them is π/6. Let w=u−v. Find |w|.
questions.solution: Using the scalar product, u·v=|u||v|cos(π/6)=4·3·(√3/2)=6√3. Therefore |w|²=|u−v|²=|u|²−2u·v+|v|²=16−12√3+9=25−12√3, so |w|=√(25−12√3).

7. [Maximum mark: 7]

A velocity graph for 0≤t≤6 has intercepts t=0,2,4; it is positive, then negative, then positive. P travels 15 m in the first 2 s, s(2)=s(5), and ∫₂⁴v dt=−9. (a) Find s(4)−s(2). [2] (b) Find total distance in the first 5 s. [5]
questions.summary: A velocity graph for 0≤t≤6 has intercepts t=0,2,4; it is positive, then negative, then positive. P travels 15 m in the first 2 s, s(2)=s(5), and ∫₂⁴v dt=−9. (a) Find s(4)−s(2). [2]
questions.solution: (a) s(4)−s(2)=−9 m. (b) Since ∫₂⁵vdt=0, ∫₄⁵vdt=9. Distance=15+|−9|+9=33 m. This agrees with the official markscheme.

8. [Maximum mark: 16]

Let f(x)=9−x². (a) Find its x-intercepts. [2] [Diagram: rectangle PQRS under the parabola, symmetric about y-axis, OP=b.] (b) Show its area is 18b−2b³. [2] (c) Find b for maximum area. [5] Let g(x)=(x−3)²+k. (d) Show intersections satisfy 2x²−6x+k=0. [2] (e) If they intersect once, find k. [5]
questions.summary: Let f(x)=9−x². (a) Find its x-intercepts. [2] [Diagram: rectangle PQRS under the parabola, symmetric about y-axis, OP=b.] (b) Show its area is 18b−2b³. [2] (c) Find b for maximum a
questions.solution: (a) x=±3. (b) A=2b(9−b²)=18b−2b³. (c) A′=18−6b²=0 gives b=√3 and A″<0. (d) Equating f,g gives the stated quadratic. (e) Its discriminant is 36−8k=0, so k=9/2. This agrees with the official markscheme.

9. [Maximum mark: 13]

Z~N(0,1), P(Z<−1.6)=a and P(Z>2.4)=b. [Normal curve with tails a and b.] (a) Find P(−1.6<Z<2.4). [2] (b) Given Z>−1.6, find P(Z<2.4). [4] X~N(m,s²), P(X<1)=a. (c) Write the standardized value for x=1. [1] Also P(X>2)=b. (d) Find s. [6]
questions.summary: Z~N(0,1), P(Z<−1.6)=a and P(Z>2.4)=b. [Normal curve with tails a and b.] (a) Find P(−1.6<Z<2.4). [2] (b) Given Z>−1.6, find P(Z<2.4). [4] X~N(m,s²), P(X<1)=a. (c) Write the standar
questions.solution: (a) 1−a−b. (b) (1−a−b)/(1−a). (c) −1.6. (d) (1−m)/s=−1.6 and (2−m)/s=2.4; subtraction gives 1/s=4, hence s=1/4. This agrees with the official markscheme.

10. [Maximum mark: 17]

Consider f(x)=√x sin(πx/4) and g(x)=√x for x≥0. Their first intersection is x=0. (a) Find the two smallest non-zero intersection x-values. [5] They form uₙ=a+bn, n≥1. (b) Find a,b. [4] (c) P is the 21st intersection; find P. [4] [Diagram: f and the reflection of g in the x-axis enclose shading to x=158.] (d) Give an integral for the shaded area. [4]
questions.summary: Consider f(x)=√x sin(πx/4) and g(x)=√x for x≥0. Their first intersection is x=0. (a) Find the two smallest non-zero intersection x-values. [5] They form uₙ=a+bn, n≥1. (b) Find a,b. [4
questions.solution: For x>0, f(x)=g(x) gives √x sin(πx/4)=√x, so sin(πx/4)=1. (a) Thus πx/4=π/2+2πk and the first two non-zero values are 2 and 10. (b) uₙ=2+8(n−1)=−6+8n, so a=−6,b=8. (c) Counting (0,0) as the first intersection, the 21st uses u₂₀=154, hence P=(154,√154). (d) The shaded area is ∫₀¹⁵⁸√x[1+sin(πx/4)]dx. This agrees with the official markscheme.
